newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says policy determined by domestic economy.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says policy determined by domestic economy.

text.p: The Bank of Japan's monetary policy will be determined by the condition of the domestic economy, BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday.

Asked whether Tuesday's decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to tighten credit would affect Japan's monetary policy, Matsushita said: "Each nation sets its monetary policy by appropriately judging its domestic economic conditions."
He added that rather than reacting to a particular policy change by another nation, it was important to monitor the effect that the change has on Japan's economy.

Matsushita said the Fed must have made Tuesday's decision after judging that inflationary risks in the United States were gradually increasing, and also in order to achieve sustainable growth with stable prices.
Asked about a recent case in which a Japanese bank's debt rating was cut, Matsushita said: "It is premature to discuss steps to support such banks which issue debentures."

The market yields of Nippon Credit Bank debentures have been under upward pressure since Moody's Investors Service cut its rating for the bank's debentures last week to what is considered junk-bond status.
Matsushita said he would not comment on individual bank credit ratings, but added that the bank in question had a restructuring plan which will gain the market's confidence.

Matsushita added that he expected the bank's plan to include drastic measures, such as sales of real estate, closure of some branches and cutting back on workers, which would allow the bank to get rid of a substantial amount of bad loans.
But Matsushita said that, on the whole, Japanese banks were making progress in resolving their bad loans.

He said the efforts at individual financial institutions were important, but added the central bank would provide liquidity support if needed in order to ensure the stability of Japan's financial system.
The BOJ will continue to guide the key money market rate below the official discount rate on average, Matsushita said.

Asked what he meant by on average, he said it was what the market naturally regarded as on average. He did not elaborate and did not give a specific time frame for over which the average would be calculated.
"It (providing a time frame) would prevent the BOJ from conducting market operations smoothly through a dialogue with the market," Matsushita said.
